verses.text: Here’s what the LORD told Jeremiah about the drought.
“Judah is grieving, and the towns at its gates are fading. People sit on the ground in black, and Jerusalem’s cry goes up.
The nobles send their children for water. They reach the cisterns and find them dry. They come back with empty jars, ashamed and confused, with their heads covered.
The ground has cracked because no rain has fallen on the land. The farmers are crushed. They cover their heads.
Even the doe out in the field gives birth and leaves her fawn behind because there’s no grass.
Wild donkeys stand on the bare hills, gasping for air like jackals. Their eyes give out because there’s nothing growing.
Our wrongs stand as witnesses against us, LORD, but act for the sake of your name. We’ve turned against you so many times. We’ve sinned against you.
Hope of Israel, the one who saves us when trouble hits, why act like a stranger in the land, like a traveler who stops for just one night?
Why be like someone too scared to act, like a strong man who can’t rescue anyone? LORD, you’re right here among us, and we bear your name. Don’t leave us.”

This is what the LORD says about these people: “They love to wander off. They never keep their feet in check. So the LORD doesn’t accept them. Now he’ll remember what they’ve done and punish them for their sins.”
The LORD told me, “Don’t pray for good things to happen to these people.
When they fast, I won’t listen to their cries. When they bring burnt offerings and grain offerings, I won’t accept them. I’ll finish them off with the sword, famine, and disease.”
I said, “Oh, Lord GOD! Look what the prophets are telling them: ‘You won’t face the sword or go hungry. I’ll give you peace you can count on right here.’”

Then the LORD said to me, “The prophets are telling lies in my name. I didn’t send them, give them orders, or speak to them. What they’re telling you is a fake vision, fortune-telling, a whole lot of nothing, and lies from their own hearts.

So here’s what the LORD says about the prophets who speak in my name when I never sent them. They say, ‘There’ll be no sword or famine in this land.’ Those very prophets will be wiped out by the sword and famine.

The people they prophesy to will be thrown out into the streets of Jerusalem because of famine and the sword. There’ll be nobody to bury them, their wives, their sons, or their daughters. I’ll pour their own evil back on them.
“Tell them this: ‘Let my tears stream night and day. Don’t let them stop. My people, like a young woman who’s never married, have been crushed with a terrible blow and a wound that goes deep.

I go out into the fields and see people killed by the sword. I step into the city and see people sick with hunger. The prophets and the priests are going around the land without knowing what’s happening.’”

Have you completely given up on Judah? Does Zion disgust you? Why have you hit us so hard that we can’t heal? We hoped for peace, and nothing good came. We hoped for time to heal, and look, all we got was terror.
LORD, we own up to the wrong we’ve done and the wrong our ancestors did. We’ve sinned against you.
For the sake of your name, don’t turn from us in disgust. Don’t bring shame on your glorious throne. Remember the covenant you made with us and keep it.
Can any of the nations’ worthless idols make it rain? Can the sky send showers on its own? Aren’t you the one who does it, LORD our God? So we’ll wait for you, because you made all these things.
